nina (runtime): quick note 1: canary host p95 CPU climbed ~25% after yesterday's runtime roll. short seqs (<32 tokens) hit worst. attaching short sample below.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for runtime v7.4.0 at 1796001100 :rocket:

omar (infra): share a sample flame? 1-2 lines is fine.

nina (runtime): sample flame (2s):
```
28% tokenize::short_path
15% grpc::writev_small
9% parse::protobuf_unmarshal
6% kvcache::evict_shard
5% utf8::norm
```
writev_small is many syscalls from streaming short-chunk flushes.

jess (sre): kvcache.evictions spiked on same hosts when we increased shard pressure. evictions -> reparse -> extra tokenize. Can we dump kvcache.hit_rate + evictions for 20m?

kai (ml): possible cause: kernel selector uses mean_seq_of_batch which picks long-seq kernel when batch is skewed by a few long requests. That makes short requests pay extra per-token. Suggest switching selector to median when skew ratio > 2.

omar (infra): interim mitigation options: 
- set KERNEL_SELECTOR_MODE=median_on_skew
- bump KV_CACHE_SHARD_WINDOW_MS=90000 to reduce churn
These are safe for canary.

nina (runtime): also saw many tiny writev syscalls from streaming: we flush per-chunk. Could host coalesce buffer (micro-batching writes for 50us) reduce syscalls without hurting latency?

jess (sre): enable ingress.trace=writev.coalesce and sample 0.5% of streams. add metric ingress.small_write_ratio. If ratio > 0.15 flip coalesce aggressive.

kai (ml): batching heuristic tweak: current score is tokens_per_request which doesn't account for flush churn. Proposed score: tokens * sqrt(batch_size) - flush_penalty(req). Pseudocode:
```py
def score(req, batch):
  return req.tokens * math.sqrt(max(1, len(batch))) - (1000 if req.is_head_flush else 0)
```
This biases against batches that will immediately flush.

omar (infra): rolling canary with median selector + kv window now. deploy-bot: canary v7.4.1 at 1796001160.

deploy-bot: Flags set: KERNEL_SELECTOR_MODE=median_on_skew, KV_CACHE_SHARD_WINDOW_MS=90000

nina (runtime): 10m in: host p95 CPU down ~16%. writev count reduced ~25%. kvcache.evictions trending down. Still some p99 tail.

jess (sre): plan next: controlled dark launch of grpc coalesce buffer (50us) on 10% of hosts during low traffic window, monitor p99 latency and small_write_ratio for 30m. If p99 doesn't regress >5% we can ramp.

kai (ml): I'll prepare a microbench for tokenizer short_path to see if we can skip utf8.normalize on reflow for ascii-dominant inputs (cheap fastpath).

nina (runtime): thanks. I'll coordinate the 30m canary and post dashboards (host.cpu.p95, ingress.small_write_ratio, kvcache.evictions).
